epic.title: Example: sign-in for a small web app
epic.goal: An example epic to show the shape of the ledger: tasks in waves, a dependency, an open decision with options, and a review subtask for a department agent. Read it, then withdraw or replace it.

tasks.title: Add a sign-in endpoint with hashed passwords

acceptance.expect: A correct password signs in, a wrong one is refused with 401, and the stored hash never equals the password. Changing the hash check to always pass makes a test fail.

tasks.title: Send password-reset emails

acceptance.check: Run tests/test_reset.py against the email provider's test mode.
acceptance.expect: A reset request for a known address sends one email with a single-use link; an unknown address sends nothing and gets the same response.

tasks.needsSam: Creates the email provider account once PR-D01 is ruled.

tasks.title: Code review of the sign-in epic

acceptance.check: Read the covered tasks' files at their landed commits for correctness, data loss and security.
acceptance.expect: The evidence names every covered file with a verdict, clean or finding N (a clean resting on a guard names it); each problem found is a finding with a pointer.

decisions.question: Which email provider sends the password-reset emails?
decisions.recommendation: A transactional email service with a free tier and a test mode, so reset emails can be tested without sending real mail.
decisions.source: Example decision, filed with the example epic

options.label: Transactional service
options.detail: A hosted email API with a test mode. Small monthly cost past the free tier.

options.label: Our own SMTP server
options.detail: No vendor, but deliverability and spam filtering are on us.

options.label: No email for now
options.detail: Resets go through support by hand until there are users who need it.
